title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 47
paragraphs: I myself saw these mines, and by far the most marvelous of them were those the Phoenicians discovered, who made the first settlement on this island with Thasus; and the island took the name it now has from this Thasus the Phoenician. These Phoenician mines are in the part of Thasos between the places called Aenyra and Coenyra, and opposite Samothrace, where there is a great mountain that has been entirely turned up in the search for metal. So much for that matter; and the Thasians, at the king's command, both razed their walls and brought all their ships to Abdera.
